content.text:
The school publishes detailed A Level results, but I couldn't find a recent overall figure for its IGCSE results.

**A Level results**

- **2026:**
58% of results were A*-A, improving even further on last year's results by 9.4%.

The "9.4%" probably means a relative increase, since 58% is only 4 percentage points above the 2025 figure.
- **2025:**

This year's record cohort of 29 candidates included 22 graduating from Year 13 and 7 accelerated learners taking A-levels early. Across all entries, 54% of grades were A* or A, and 74% were A*–B, with a 100% pass rate. By comparison, the UK average for A*/A grades in 2025 was just 28%.
By subject, 2025 included
100% A*-B grades in Art (with an incredible 70% of our students earning an A* grade in the subject!)
and
100% of our students taking A-level Maths early awarded A* grades.
The British School of Nanjing in China had 92% of grades at A*-A and a 100% pass rate.
A record 100% of students' A-levels being awarded A/A* grades
The school's pass rate is consistently given as 100%. Its website says that
every year, 100% of our students pass their A-levels. And in 2025, 74% achieved an A*.

That 74% A* figure clashes with the school's own 2025 results article, which gives 74% as the share of A*–B grades. The detailed article is probably more accurate, so I'd treat "74% A*" with caution.

**IGCSE results**

- The latest overall figure I found is from **2020**:
a fantastic 58% of IGCSEs being awarded A/A* grades.
- **Top individual results:**
In the last three years, two of our students have achieved the highest IGCSE language scores in the world.
These were in Mandarin. In 2023,
two of our students achieved the highest examination marks in China, whilst one student achieved the highest examination mark in the world!
One of those was the
Highest Mark in China Award in IGCSE Geography

.

**Universities:** For the Class of 2025,
12 out of 23 students have received offers from TOP 100 global universities, making up 52.2%

All these figures come from the school or Nord Anglia, the group that owns it, so they haven't been independently checked. For a full breakdown, especially recent IGCSE grades, it's best to ask the admissions office directly.
